question.problem: In his first season in the youth soccer league, Fernando scored $8$ goals. In his second season, he scored $250%$ of the number of goals he made in the first season. How many goals did Fernando score in his second season?
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we can use the formula:

$$
\text{part}=\text{percentage}\times \text{whole}
$$

In our case, the whole is the number of goals Fernando scored in the first season, which is $8$ goals. The percentage is $250%,$ and the part is the number of goals Fernando scored in the second season.

**Method 1**

First, we convert the percentage to a decimal:

$$
250%=250÷100=2.5
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =250%\times 8 \\  & =2.5\times 8 \\  & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $250%$ of $8$ is $20.$ So, Fernando scored $20$ goals in his second season.

**Method 2**

First, we convert the percentage to a fraction:

$$
250%=\frac{250}{100}=\frac{250÷50}{100÷50}=\frac{5}{2}
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =250%\times 8 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\times 8 \\  & =\frac{40}{2} \\  & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $250%$ of $8$ is $20.$ So, Fernando scored $20$ goals in his second season.
